The Nafiu Gombe-led Board of Trustees of the African Democratic Congress has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission to immediately enforce the November 5, 2026 judgment of the Federal High Court concerning the party’s leadership dispute. The Board also called on INEC to remove the names of Senator David Mark and Rauf Aregbesola from its records as the party’s leaders and delist candidates uploaded to its portal by the Mark-led leadership. The BoT, in a statement issued by its Chairman, Chief Rufus Ikanmi, said the judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, filed by Hon. Nafi’u Bala Gombe against the ADC and four others, remained valid and binding. Ikanmi said, “The judgment of the Honourable Court is valid, binding, and subsisting. It has not been stayed, varied, or set aside by any superior court. INEC, as a statutory body bound by the rule of law, has a constitutional duty to give full effect to it without further delay.” He urged the commission to recognise and deal only with the leadership headed by Gombe, which he said was affirmed by the court. David Mark and Rauf Aregbesola-led leadership from its records as leaders of the African Democratic Congress; “Remove and delist all candidates uploaded to the INEC portal by the said leadership, as such uploads were done in clear violation of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as Amended), Electoral Act 2022 and the party’s constitution. “Recognise and deal only with the lawful leadership of the Party under the leadership of Hon Nafiu Bala Gombe, as affirmed by the Federal High Court.” The BoT also urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and other persons allegedly acting with the Mark-led leadership to suspend campaign activities, rallies and public engagements organised in the name of the ADC pending compliance with the judgment. Coalition urges Atiku, Obi, others to back consensus candidate 2027: APC, ADC clash over Katsina insecurity, governance 2027: Atiku demands independent audit of INEC’s AI system “Any continued defiance of the judgment of the Federal High Court amounts to contempt of court and a direct assault on constitutional democracy and the rule of law,” Ikanmi said. The board called on party members and supporters to remain calm and law-abiding, adding that it was committed to peace, unity and the constitutional order of the party. On November 5, Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the leadership of the ADC led by former Senate President David Mark and invalidated decisions taken by the party under the leadership. The court ruled in favour of Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former Deputy National Chairman of the party (North-East), who had challenged the emergence of Mark and other members of the interim National Working Committee following the resignation of former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu. However, the Mark-led ADC has appealed the judgement. The party also disclosed that it had filed an application for a stay of execution of the judgment pending the hearing and determination of the appeal. Efforts to get the the Chief Press Secretary to the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Dayo Oketola were not successful as of the time of filling this report. However, a report by Arise News on Thursday, citing a senior official of the commission, said the continued listing was connected to a subsisting Notice of Appeal and an application for a Stay of Execution relating to the judgment. The report added that the commission could not disregard the pending appellate proceedings while considering requests for recognition arising from the ruling.
